System description:
# Case: Tesla Model X with Autopilot (Mountain View, California, 2018)

Source: NTSB Highway Accident Report HAR-20/01. This is a description of the system and its use before the crash. It does not include the investigation findings.

## System
A 2017 Tesla Model X has Autopilot, a SAE Level 2 partial driving automation feature. It combines Traffic-Aware Cruise Control (TACC) and Autosteer (lane keeping). The driver stays responsible for driving and monitoring the road.

## Main parts
- Sensors: a forward-facing camera, a forward-facing radar and ultrasonic sensors.
- Vision processing: a camera-based system detects lane markings, vehicles and some objects ahead.
- TACC: holds a speed set by the driver, follows a vehicle ahead at a chosen gap, and returns to the set speed when no vehicle is ahead.
- Autosteer: keeps the vehicle in its lane using lane markings and the path of the vehicle ahead.
- Forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking are available as separate features.
- Driver monitoring: steering torque is used to check that the driver's hands are on the wheel, with visual and audible alerts if no hands are detected for a period of time.

## People
- The driver sets the cruising speed, turns Autopilot on, and is told to keep hands on the wheel and watch the road.
- Other road users and road workers share the highway. Road agencies maintain road markings and safety hardware such as barriers and crash attenuators.

## Operating context
Busy multi-lane freeway with high-occupancy-vehicle (HOV) lanes, exits and interchanges, lane markings of different quality, and traffic that changes in speed.

goals.text: Set the cruising speed.
Turn Autopilot on.
Keep hands on the steering wheel.
Watch the road and remain responsible for driving.
Reach the destination safely.
Assist with longitudinal and lateral driving through TACC and Autosteer.
Operate as a Level 2 assistance feature while leaving driving responsibility with the driver.
Provide data from the forward-facing camera, forward-facing radar, and ultrasonic sensors.
Use camera-based processing to detect lane markings, vehicles, and some objects ahead.
Maintain the speed set by the driver.
Follow a vehicle ahead at the gap chosen by the driver.
Return to the driver-set speed when there is no vehicle ahead.
Keep the vehicle in its lane using lane markings and the path of the vehicle ahead.
Warn the driver of a forward collision hazard.
Apply automatic emergency braking for a forward collision hazard.
Use steering torque to check whether the driver's hands are on the wheel.
Provide visual and audible alerts when hands are not detected for a period of time.
Share the highway safely with the vehicle and other traffic.
Remain safe near highway traffic.
Carry out road work safely while sharing the highway.
Maintain highway road markings.
Maintain highway safety hardware, including barriers and crash attenuators.

requirements.text: The system shall detect driver unresponsiveness during Autopilot operation and, when the driver fails to respond to a takeover alert within the specified response interval, shall disengage Autopilot and issue an escalating warning.

The vision system shall retain and assess uncertain detections of stationary objects, pedestrians, and road workers in the vehicle's path, and shall issue a hazard warning or initiate a conservative speed reduction rather than treating an uncertain detection as absent.

For each supported operating condition, the collision-avoidance system shall detect a forward collision hazard and begin braking early enough to meet its specified collision-avoidance or impact-mitigation performance, as verified in representative hazard tests.

TACC shall resume the driver-set speed only when sensor data indicates that the vehicle's forward travel corridor is clear; if an object in that corridor is detected or cannot be ruled out, TACC shall not accelerate toward the set speed.

While TACC is active, the system shall limit vehicle speed to a validated safe speed for detected traffic, visibility, road-layout, and work-zone conditions, and shall reduce speed when those conditions no longer support the current speed.

When steering-torque monitoring indicates that the driver's hands are not on the wheel, the system shall issue an alert and, if hands-on-wheel status is not restored within the specified interval, shall disengage Autosteer.

Before road work begins in or adjacent to a live traffic lane, the responsible road agency shall provide and inspect traffic-control measures that separate or protect workers and equipment from moving traffic, and shall correct any missing or ineffective measure before work proceeds.

Autosteer shall assess lane-marking and path-estimation confidence and shall alert the driver and suspend lane-keeping control when markings are worn, obscured, conflicting, or temporary enough that the estimated lane or path fails its validated confidence criterion.

The system shall identify Autopilot as Level 2 driver assistance, state that the driver must continuously supervise and remain responsible for driving, and present this information at activation and persistently while Autopilot is engaged.

The responsible road agency shall inspect barriers and crash attenuators at locations identified by its roadway hazard assessment, repair or replace hardware that is absent or unserviceable, and provide temporary protection until repairs are complete.
